=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/attempt_journal.py:205-227 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: parse() merges entries from all trusted comments, but there is no locking, so two concurrent `append` operations that PATCH the same comment can lose entries.
  WHY: An attempt entry logged by one stage could be lost if another stage completes and PATCHes the comment in the window between the first stage's read and write (source severity MAJOR).
- scripts/implement_step_prepush_test_gate.sh:implement_prepush_test_gate_journal_blocks | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The function uses `sed` to extract the repair rules body; if the rules file contains the marker line but the rules after it are empty or missing, it succeeds silently without appending the rules.
  WHY: The repair prompt will lack the required rules for the repair turn without logging the absence as required, so it fails to guide the editor when deletions are involved (source severity NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The P1 entry schema defines failure_key as "the first 12 hex of workflow_failure_heal.fingerprint(<workflow>, <step>, error_signature(<failure text>)), else """ (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md:320). P8 reads it at line 202 and line 518, and the progress rule reads it at line 479 ("a different failure_key").
  Expected change site: The "Record attempt journal entry (implement)" step in .github/workflows/implement.yml, the review writer in scripts/review_commit_changes.sh, and _resolver_attempt_journal_append in scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh. Each should pass --failure-workflow, --failure-step and --failure-text-file to scripts/attempt_journal.py append.
  Evidence of absence: cmd_append computes failure_key only when args.failure_workflow and args.failure_text_file are both set. None of the five writer call sites (clarify.yml, plan.yml, implement.yml, review_commit_changes.sh, review_conflict_resolve.sh) passes those flags, so every entry records failure_key "". The issue says "do not shrink P1's scope". The gate result.json failures list is available as failure text in implement and review.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- HARDENING: scripts/attempt_journal.py | parse(), "newest_id = _comment_id(comment)"
  PROBLEM: If the newest trusted journal has no usable id (a GraphQL node without databaseId), newest_id is overwritten with None even though an older trusted journal has a valid id. cmd_append then POSTs a new journal comment instead of PATCHing.
  WHY: Defensive only, because today's append paths load REST comments, which always have an id. Fix: `newest_id = _comment_id(comment) or newest_id` (1 line).
- HARDENING: tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py | _run_journal_block and _render_review_editor_splice
  PROBLEM: Both call tmp.cleanup() only after the subprocess returncode assert, so a failing assert leaves the temporary directory behind (this applies to pytest and to run_all_contract_tests, called from tests/test_workspace_init.py:345).
  WHY: Fix: wrap the body in "with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_name:" or try/finally (4 lines).
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
